title: The Fly and the Draught-Mule
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Fly sat on one of the shafts of a cart and said to the Mule who was pulling it, "How slow you are! Do mend your pace, or I shall have to use my sting as a goad." The Mule was not in the least disturbed. "Behind me, in the cart," said he, "sits my master. He holds the reins, and flicks me with his whip, and him I obey, but I don't want any of your impertinence. I know when I may dawdle and when I may not."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where is the Fly sitting?
options: On the Mule's back
On the cart's wheel
On one of the shafts of a cart
On a nearby fence post

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fly complain about?
options: That the Mule is too slow
That the cart is too heavy
That the road is too rough
That the sun is too hot

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fly threaten to use as a goad?
options: Its wings
Its legs
Its voice
Its sting

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who sits behind the Mule in the cart?
options: A second mule
His master
A group of travellers
No one at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the master control the Mule?
options: He calls out commands loudly
He walks beside the Mule and guides him by hand
He holds the reins and flicks him with his whip
He rings a small bell to signal directions

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whom does the Mule say he obeys?
options: His master
The Fly
Whoever speaks first
No one at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Mule call the Fly's demand?
options: Good advice
A fair warning
A harmless joke
Impertinence

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Mule "not in the least disturbed" by the Fly's threat?
options: He cannot feel the Fly's sting at all
He recognizes that the Fly has no real authority over his pace
He has already agreed to speed up before the Fly spoke
He believes the Fly is joking rather than serious

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "dawdle" mean in "I know when I may dawdle and when I may not"?
options: To rest completely and stop moving
To run at full speed
To move slowly or waste time
To change direction suddenly

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Only those with real authority over you can rightfully expect to be obeyed
Flies are more dangerous to mules than most people realize
Speed is always more important than following instructions
Masters should never trust their mules to set their own pace

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fly tell the Mule to do?
options: Turn down a different road
Stop and rest
Wait for the master's signal
Mend his pace

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two things does the master use to control the Mule?
options: A rope and a bell
The reins and a whip
His voice and a stick
A saddle and spurs

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Mule say he knows about his own pace?
options: That he should always move as fast as possible
That only the Fly can decide his speed
When he may dawdle and when he may not
That the cart is too heavy to go any faster

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Mule distinguish between the master's whip and the Fly's sting?
options: One comes from someone with real authority over him, and the other does not
The whip hurts less than the sting would
The Fly has never actually touched him before
The master has forbidden the Mule from responding to insects

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fly seem to misunderstand about its own position?
options: It assumes the Mule cannot hear its warning
It assumes the cart is going the wrong direction
It assumes the master will side with the Mule regardless
It assumes its threat carries the same weight as the master's authority

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "goad" mean in "use my sting as a goad"?
options: Something used to measure distance
Something used to prod or urge into action
Something used to signal danger
Something used to attract attention

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Fly successfully makes the Mule move faster
A Mule throws the Fly off the cart in anger
A Fly's threat to speed up the Mule is calmly dismissed, since only the master has real control over him
The master sides with the Fly against the Mule
